root_cause.text: On x86, the IOMMU Shared Virtual Addressing (SVA) feature shares CPU page tables that include kernel mappings, and the kernel lacks a mechanism to notify the IOMMU when kernel page table pages are freed and reused, causing the IOMMU to cache stale entries that can be exploited for use-after-free or write-after-free attacks.
root_cause.evidence: "The Linux kernel currently lacks a notification mechanism for kernel page table changes, specifically when page table pages are freed and reused. The IOMMU driver is only notified of changes to user virtual address mappings. This can cause the IOMMU's internal caches to retain stale entries for kernel VA." – from the CVE description and commit message. The patch disables SVA on x86 (CONFIG_X86) to mitigate this until a proper notification mechanism is added.

intent_record.intent_summary: Explicitly reject SVA device binding on x86 architectures as unsupported.
intent_record.what: Added an early return of -EOPNOTSUPP in iommu_sva_bind_device when CONFIG_X86 is enabled, before acquiring the iommu_sva_lock.
intent_record.how: On x86 systems, the function immediately fails with -EOPNOTSUPP, preventing any further SVA binding logic from executing. Non-x86 systems remain unaffected.

grouping_result.intent: Explicitly reject SVA device binding on x86 architectures as unsupported.

candidates.rationale: This line begins the SVA binding critical section without any architecture check. On x86, the IOMMU SVA feature shares kernel page tables without notification when pages are freed, leading to use-after-free. The lack of a guard to reject SVA on x86 makes this statement directly responsible for permitting the vulnerable path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code in this commit primarily restructures PASID and sva domain management by introducing iommu_mm_data. It does not include any notification mechanism for IOMMU when kernel page table pages are freed, which is the core missing component described in the vulnerability root cause. Since the vulnerable construct (lack of notification) is absent from the functions shown, has_bug is false.
